initialize.instructions:
Use Ashlr tools for scoped, token-efficient repository retrieval: orient/tree for structure, grep for relevant symbols, then read the required files or ranges.
Compact or summarized results are navigation aids. Retrieve omitted source before editing or verifying behavior; never treat omitted content as absent.
Preserve task requirements, AGENTS.md instructions, authorization boundaries, citations, exact error details and verification evidence. Expand retrieval when any of these are missing.
Use diff-format edits and focused tests. Savings estimates apply only to the tool output actually shortened; model quality, task success and token savings require separate evidence.

tools.name: ashlr__glob
tools.description: Token-efficient glob pattern matching. Returns compressed output instead of raw file lists: ≤20 matches listed verbatim; >20 matches grouped by top-level directory with counts and sample paths. Honors .gitignore automatically inside git repos (uses `git ls-files`), otherwise walks the filesystem while skipping node_modules, dist, build, .git, .next, .cache, .turbo, __pycache__, .venv. Replaces the native Glob tool — produces 70-90% fewer tokens on large repos.

tools.name: ashlr__tree
tools.description: Token-efficient project structure view. One call returns a Unicode box-drawing tree with per-directory size/file-count and optional per-file LOC. Honors .gitignore automatically inside git repos, otherwise skips a standard exclusion set (node_modules, dist, build, .git, .next, .cache, .turbo, __pycache__, .venv). Replaces the 3-5 orientation calls (ls -la + find + multiple Reads) Claude Code normally makes when opening a repo.

pattern.description: Only include files matching this regex (e.g. '\\.ts$')

exclude.description: Directory names to skip (default: node_modules, dist, build, .git, .next, .cache, .turbo, __pycache__, .venv, .DS_Store)

sizes.description: Include file sizes shown as B/KB/MB (default: true)

loc.description: Include line counts for text files (default: false; skips files over 2 MB)

maxEntries.description: Hard cap on entries returned (default: 500). When exceeded, per-dir truncation with count.

tools.name: ashlr__ls
tools.description: Gitignore-aware directory listing. Compact columnar output with elision past maxEntries (default 80). Set bypassSummary:true to see all entries.

path.description: Directory to list (absolute or cwd-relative). Default '.'

tools.name: ashlr__diff
tools.description: Fast adaptive git diff. Use instead of native Bash 'git diff | cat' when reviewing changes — avoids dumping thousands of lines into context. Compresses by auto-selecting stat-only (>500 changed lines), stat+hottest-hunks (100–500), or full patch (<100); typical savings 60–95% on large diffs. Accepts any git ref plus pseudo-refs 'staged', 'unstaged', 'working'. For refactor/rename reviews use ashlr__diff_semantic instead.

ref.description: Git ref to diff against (default: HEAD~1). Also accepts 'staged' / 'unstaged' / 'working'.

path.description: Limit to path(s) — file or dir

mode.description: 'stat' (files + lines only) · 'summary' (stat + hottest hunks) · 'full' (default: adaptive — stat if huge, summary if moderate, full if small)

bypassSummary.description: If true, skip LLM summarization and return the full compacted diff.

tools.name: ashlr__webfetch
tools.description: Token-efficient URL fetcher. Aggressively extracts article text from HTML (title + main content, strips nav/scripts/styles), pretty-prints + array-elides JSON, byte-caps plain text. Default cap 100 KB vs native WebFetch which is uncapped. Use instead of WebFetch when you want article content — saves 60-95% tokens on typical pages.

prompt.description: What you're looking for — included as a hint in the output header

tools.name: ashlr__read
tools.description: Read a file with snipCompact truncation (head + tail, elided middle). Use instead of native Read when the file is >2KB — avoids returning the full payload; compresses by preserving only the structurally significant head and tail; typical savings 60–90% on large files. Pass bypassSummary:true to get the full file when you need it.

bypassSummary.description: Skip LLM summarization, return snipCompact-truncated content (default: false)

mode.description: auto (default): use AST skeleton for large wired-lang files; ast: force skeleton; snip: force snipCompact head+tail

tools.name: ashlr__flush
tools.description: Flush all queued ashlr__edit writes to disk immediately and return a summary of what was committed. Use when you need to read a file you just edited, or at the end of a multi-edit sequence.

tools.name: ashlr__edit_structural
tools.description: Rename a symbol with AST awareness (one file or N files). Use instead of native Edit when renaming variables/functions/types — avoids accidental matches in strings/comments. Compresses by returning only a rename summary; typical savings 80–95%. operation='rename': file-local. operation='rename-cross-file': across rootDir. operation='extract-function': extract byte-range to new function. Supports .ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx. dryRun=true previews. Use ashlr__edit for literal edits.

path.description: Absolute or cwd-relative file path (rename, extract-function)

name.description: Current identifier name to rename (rename, rename-cross-file)

dryRun.description: If true, return the planned edits without writing (default false)

force.description: Bypass shadowing + collision guards for rename (default false)

anchorFile.description: Absolute path of the file that declares + exports the symbol (rename-cross-file). When set, only files that import the symbol from this file are renamed — unrelated local same-named identifiers are left alone.

maxFiles.description: Hard cap on candidate files for cross-file rename (default 200). Beyond this the rename is truncated and a warning is emitted.

start.description: Byte offset start of range to extract (extract-function)

end.description: Byte offset end of range to extract (extract-function)

tools.name: ashlr__rename_file
tools.description: Rename (move) a source file AND update every import specifier in the project that resolved to it. Handles extension elision ('./foo' → './bar'), directory-index resolution ('./foo' when foo/index.ts), and skips bare package specifiers. Refuses if 'to' already exists, 'to's parent directory is missing, paths escape cwd, or either path is a binary file. Supports dryRun. Complements ashlr__edit_structural (which renames identifiers, not module paths).

from.description: Current file path (absolute or cwd-relative). Must exist.

to.description: New file path (absolute or cwd-relative). Must NOT exist; parent dir must exist.

dryRun.description: If true, list planned edits without writing or renaming (default false).

maxFiles.description: Hard cap on importer candidate files (default 200). Beyond this the scan truncates with a warning.

roots.description: Limit the importer scan to these subdirectories (absolute or cwd-relative). Default: process.cwd().

tools.name: ashlr__search_replace_regex
tools.description: Regex-based bulk substitution across files in one call. Use instead of native Edit when patterns are mechanical (X→Y across many call sites) — native Edit doesn't support regex. Compresses by returning a per-file match-count summary; typical savings 80–95%. Global flag is implicit; supports i/m/s/u; capture groups ($1, $2, $&) in replacement. Use dryRun=true to preview. For literal single-file edits use ashlr__edit. For AST-aware renames use ashlr__edit_structural.

pattern.description: Regex source (e.g. 'logger\\.info\\('). Anchors, classes, and capture groups are all supported.

flags.description: Optional flags subset — i (case-insensitive), m (multiline), s (dotall), u (unicode). The g flag is always implicit.

include.description: ripgrep-style glob patterns to include (e.g. ['src/**/*.ts']). When omitted, all files under roots are candidates.

dryRun.description: If true, return the planned change set (per-file match counts) without writing. Default false.

maxFiles.description: Hard cap on candidate files scanned. Default 200. Overflow is truncated with a warning (not a refusal).

maxMatchesPerFile.description: Hard cap on replacements per file. Default 100. Extra matches are left in place and flagged as capped.

roots.description: Search roots (cwd-relative or absolute). Default: [process.cwd()]. Each is cwd-clamped.

tools.name: ashlr__websearch
tools.description: Token-efficient web search wrapper. Deduplicates results by domain, truncates snippets to ~500 chars, and synthesizes a 1-paragraph summary when more than 3 results are returned. Use instead of WebSearch to save 40-80% tokens on search result payloads. Args: query (required), maxResults (default 5), summarize (default true).

summarize.description: Whether to synthesize a summary paragraph (default true)

tools.name: ashlr__task_list
tools.description: Token-efficient task list viewer. Filters by status/owner, limits to max rows (default 30), and returns a compact column view: taskId, status, subject (80 chars), ageMin. Use instead of TaskList to avoid verbose task payloads. Args: status (optional filter), owner (optional filter), limit (default 30).

tools.name: ashlr__task_get
tools.description: Token-efficient single task viewer. Fetches a task by ID and snipCompacts the description if it exceeds 2KB (head + tail with elision marker). Returns: taskId, status, subject, descriptionCompact, fullLength. Use instead of TaskGet for long-description tasks. Args: taskId (required).

tools.name: ashlr__notebook_edit
tools.description: Edit a single cell in a Jupyter notebook (.ipynb). Use instead of native NotebookEdit when the notebook is >5KB or has many unrelated cells — only the edited cell and its immediate neighbors are returned, with `[N cells unchanged]` for the rest. The full notebook is never echoed. Typical savings: 65-75% on multi-cell notebooks. Args: notebookPath, cellIndex, newSource, cellType (optional: code|markdown).

notebookPath.description: Absolute or cwd-relative path to the .ipynb notebook

cellIndex.description: Zero-based index of the cell to edit

newSource.description: New source content for the cell

cellType.description: Optional: change the cell type (code or markdown)

tools.name: ashlr__grep
tools.description: Search for a pattern. Use instead of native Grep always — genome-aware when .ashlrcode/genome/ exists (returns only the most relevant pre-summarized sections + merged PRs + closed issues), falls back to ripgrep with LLM summarization for large result sets. Compresses by filtering to relevant chunks; typical savings 70–90%.

bypassSummary.description: Skip LLM summarization, return rg output as-is (default: false)

include_prs.description: Include matching merged PRs from the cloud genome. Default: true. Set to false to skip PR retrieval entirely.

include_issues.description: Include matching closed issues from the cloud genome. Default: true. Set to false to skip issue retrieval entirely.

since_days.description: Optional freshness window — drop PRs / issues older than N days. Default: undefined (no filter).

tools.name: ashlr__edit
tools.description: Single literal search/replace in one file, returns only a diff summary. Use instead of native Edit when the file is >5KB or the combined before/after is >=80 chars — avoids the full file round-trip. Compresses by returning only the changed lines; typical savings 80%. In strict mode (default) requires exactly one match. For many edits across files use ashlr__multi_edit instead. For symbol renames use ashlr__edit_structural instead.

tools.name: ashlr__write
tools.description: Write content to a file without echoing the full content back. If the file already exists, delegates to ashlr__edit (full-file replace, compact diff response). If the file is new, creates it and returns a compact acknowledgment (path, bytes, sha8). Either way, the full file content is never returned — ~80% token savings vs native Write.

filePath.description: Absolute or cwd-relative path to write (`path` is accepted too)

tools.name: ashlr__http
tools.description: HTTP fetch with compressed output. Readable-extracts main content from HTML, pretty-prints + array-elides JSON, bounded byte cap. Refuses non-http/https schemes and private hosts by default.

tools.name: ashlr__logs
tools.description: Tail a log file efficiently. Reads the last N lines (default 200), detects severity from bracketed tags, bare prefixes, JSON/logfmt level fields, and Python tracebacks, filters by level and/or ISO timestamp, and collapses runs of identical consecutive lines into '(42x) ...'. Supports glob paths. Lines with no parseable timestamp are skipped (never fatal) when 'since' is set.

since.description: ISO timestamp — only lines after this

dedupe.description: Collapse repeated consecutive lines with count (default: true)

bypassSummary.description: If true, skip LLM summarization and return the full rendered log tail.

tools.name: ashlr__sql
tools.description: Run SQL against SQLite or Postgres and get a compact, token-dense text result. Replaces the typical 3-4 Bash calls (psql / sqlite3 + parse stdout) with one tool call. Supports SELECT, DDL, DML, EXPLAIN, and a schema-introspection mode.

query.description: SQL to run (SELECT, EXPLAIN, DDL, DML — all allowed). Required unless schema:true.

connection.description: Connection URL (postgres://…) or SQLite path. If omitted, reads $DATABASE_URL, then looks for *.db / *.sqlite files in cwd.

explain.description: Wrap in EXPLAIN ANALYZE (postgres) / EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN (sqlite). Default false.

limit.description: Max rows to return in the compact output (default 20). Total row count is always reported.

schema.description: Skip the query and instead list tables, columns, and row counts. Cheaper than many \d / SHOW TABLES round-trips.

bypassSummary.description: Skip LLM summarization of long output

tools.name: ashlr__diff_semantic
tools.description: AST-aware (heuristic) git diff summarization. A 200-line rename-refactor across 20 files renders as one line. Detects: symbol renames across >= 3 files, signature-only changes, formatting-only diffs. Degrades gracefully to compact diff output when no semantic patterns are found. Use instead of ashlr__diff when reviewing refactors, renames, or large reformatting commits.

range.description: Git range to diff, e.g. 'HEAD~1..HEAD'. Default: unstaged working tree changes.

staged.description: If true, diff staged changes (--cached). Overrides range.

bypassSummary.description: Skip LLM summarization of long semantic-diff output (default: false).

tools.name: ashlr__pr
tools.description: Fetch a GitHub PR and return a compact review-ready summary (header, reviews, unresolved comments, status checks). Read-only — never approves, comments, or merges. Saves 60-90% of the tokens a raw `gh pr view` dump would cost.

repo.description: owner/repo (default: auto-detect from cwd git remote)

mode.description: 'summary' (default: decisions + unresolved + checks) | 'full' (adds diff summary) | 'thread' (just comments)

tools.name: ashlr__issue
tools.description: Fetch a GitHub issue and return a compact header + body + comment list. In 'thread' mode, each comment is rendered with snipCompact on > 500 char bodies. Read-only.

repo.description: owner/repo (default: auto-detect from cwd git remote)

tools.name: ashlr__pr_comment
tools.description: Post a comment on a GitHub PR. Pass pr:"current" to target the PR for the checked-out branch. Returns the new comment URL.

pr.description: PR number or the string "current" to target the current branch's PR

repo.description: owner/repo (default: auto-detect from cwd git remote)

tools.name: ashlr__pr_approve
tools.description: Approve a GitHub PR with an optional review body. Refuses to approve your own PR. Pass pr:"current" to target the PR for the checked-out branch.

pr.description: PR number or the string "current" to target the current branch's PR

repo.description: owner/repo (default: auto-detect from cwd git remote)

tools.name: ashlr__issue_create
tools.description: Create a new GitHub issue with title + body and optional labels/assignees. Returns the new issue number and URL.

repo.description: owner/repo (default: auto-detect from cwd git remote)

tools.name: ashlr__issue_close
tools.description: Close a GitHub issue with an optional closing comment and reason (completed|not_planned).

repo.description: owner/repo (default: auto-detect from cwd git remote)

tools.name: ashlr__genome_propose
tools.description: Queue a proposed update to a named genome section. Fire-and-forget: the proposal is appended to the pending queue and will be merged into the genome on the next ashlr__genome_consolidate call. Use this to record project decisions, new strategies, architectural discoveries, or lessons learned so they persist across sessions.

section.description: Section path relative to .ashlrcode/genome, e.g. 'knowledge/decisions.md' or 'strategies/active.md'

content.description: Proposed content (full section replace OR appended block; see 'operation')

operation.description: How to apply the content (default: append)

tools.name: ashlr__genome_consolidate
tools.description: Merge pending proposals into the genome. Without `model` (and without $ASHLR_LLM_URL) runs a deterministic sequential-apply; with an LLM configured by $ASHLR_LLM_URL it merges conflicting proposals for the same section.

model.description: Pass 'none' to force offline sequential-apply, or any other value (for example 'llm') to merge with the LLM configured by $ASHLR_LLM_URL (default local LM Studio at 127.0.0.1:1234). The value is never used as an endpoint. If omitted, uses the LLM only when $ASHLR_LLM_URL or $ASHLR_LLM_KEY is set.

tools.name: ashlr__genome_status
tools.description: Show pending proposals and recent mutations for the current genome. Compact report suitable for inline context.

tools.name: ashlr__multi_edit
tools.description: Many edits across multiple files in one atomic call. Use instead of N separate Edit or ashlr__edit calls when touching more than one file — N round-trips collapse to 1, with full rollback on any failure. Compresses by returning one consolidated diff summary; typical savings (N−1) × per-call overhead. For a single file use ashlr__edit instead. For symbol renames use ashlr__edit_structural instead.

edits.description: Ordered list of edits to apply atomically.

path.description: Absolute or cwd-relative file path. File must exist.

search.description: Exact string to find in the file.

strict.description: Default true: require exactly one match (error if 0 or 2+). Pass false to replace all occurrences.

tools.name: ashlr__orient
tools.description: Meta-orientation tool. Answers 'how does X work here?' in a single call: runs a project tree scan, derives keywords from your query, discovers relevant files (genome retriever if .ashlrcode/genome/ exists, else ripgrep), snipCompacts them, and asks a local LLM for a ≤600-char synthesis plus a suggested next tool call. Replaces 3-5 round-trips (tree + grep + multiple reads). Read-only.

query.description: Question about the codebase: 'how does auth work', 'where is X defined', 'what's the deploy flow'

depth.description: 'quick' (1 tool call + 3 reads, ~2s) | 'thorough' (tree + grep + 6 reads, ~4s, default)

tools.name: ashlr__bash
tools.description: Run a shell command. Use instead of native Bash when the command produces verbose output (git log, test runners, npm install, find, ps). Auto-compresses stdout > 2KB and emits compact structured summaries for common commands (git status, ls, find, npm ls). stderr is never compressed. Refuses catastrophic patterns; use ashlr__read for cat. Typical savings 60–90% on verbose commands.

bypassSummary.description: Skip LLM summarization of long output

tools.name: ashlr__bash_start
tools.description: Spawn a long-running shell command in the background and return a session id. Use ashlr__bash_tail to poll incremental output, ashlr__bash_stop to kill, ashlr__bash_list to enumerate. Ideal for watchers, tails, long builds, and anything where streaming >> one-shot.

tools.name: ashlr__bash_tail
tools.description: Read new stdout/stderr since the last poll for a background session. Auto-compresses the tail window when > 2KB. If wait_ms > 0, blocks (event-driven) until output arrives or the process exits, up to that ceiling.

wait_ms.description: Block up to N ms for new output (default 1500; 0 = return immediately)

tools.name: ashlr__bash_stop
tools.description: Kill a background session by id. Sends SIGTERM (configurable) and escalates to SIGKILL after 2s if still alive.

signal.description: Default SIGTERM; escalates to SIGKILL after 2s

tools.name: ashlr__bash_list
tools.description: List active background sessions: id | pid | started | cumulative bytes | command.

tools.name: ashlr__test
tools.description: Run a test suite and return structured, token-efficient failure output. Supports bun test, vitest, jest, pytest, go test, and a generic fallback. Parses runner output into pass/fail/skip counts plus per-failure file:line + message + stack — eliminating the read-source-fix-rerun loop that wastes 25–30% of tokens on test-driven workflows.

command.description: Full command to run verbatim (e.g. 'bun test src/foo.test.ts'). Overrides runner + files.

cwd.description: Working directory (default: cwd). Must be inside the current cwd.

files.description: Specific test file paths to pass to the runner.

runner.description: Test runner to use. 'auto' detects from package.json / go.mod / pytest.ini (default: auto).

failuresOnly.description: Return only failure details, not per-test pass output (default: true).

bypassSummary.description: Show all failures instead of truncating at 2 inline (default: false).

watch.description: Run tests once, then fork into a background watch session that re-runs on .ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx/.py/.go file changes (debounced 200ms). Returns a session id — stream output with ashlr__bash_tail, stop with ashlr__bash_stop (default: false).

grep.description: Test name filter (informational label stored on the watch session).

tools.name: ashlr__savings
tools.description: Show estimated tokens and cost saved by ashlr tools in the current session and lifetime totals. Use instead of manually counting tool calls to measure ashlr efficiency.

tools.name: ashlr__ask
tools.description: Single-tool entry point for ashlr. Accepts a natural-language question and auto-routes to the correct underlying tool (ashlr__read, ashlr__grep, ashlr__orient, ashlr__tree, or ashlr__glob) using deterministic rules — no LLM in the routing step. Output always starts with a one-line trace showing which tool fired and why.

maxFiles.description: Hard cap on candidate files scanned. Default 200. Overflow is truncated with a warning (not a refusal).

maxMatchesPerFile.description: Hard cap on replacements per file. Default 100. Extra matches are left in place and flagged as capped.

roots.description: Search roots (cwd-relative or absolute). Default: [process.cwd()]. Each is cwd-clamped.

toolsWithPipe.name: ashlr__websearch
toolsWithPipe.description: Token-efficient web search wrapper. Deduplicates results by domain, truncates snippets to ~500 chars, and synthesizes a 1-paragraph summary when more than 3 results are returned. Use instead of WebSearch to save 40-80% tokens on search result payloads. Args: query (required), maxResults (default 5), summarize (default true).

summarize.description: Whether to synthesize a summary paragraph (default true)

toolsWithPipe.name: ashlr__task_list
toolsWithPipe.description: Token-efficient task list viewer. Filters by status/owner, limits to max rows (default 30), and returns a compact column view: taskId, status, subject (80 chars), ageMin. Use instead of TaskList to avoid verbose task payloads. Args: status (optional filter), owner (optional filter), limit (default 30).

toolsWithPipe.name: ashlr__task_get
toolsWithPipe.description: Token-efficient single task viewer. Fetches a task by ID and snipCompacts the description if it exceeds 2KB (head + tail with elision marker). Returns: taskId, status, subject, descriptionCompact, fullLength. Use instead of TaskGet for long-description tasks. Args: taskId (required).

toolsWithPipe.name: ashlr__notebook_edit
toolsWithPipe.description: Edit a single cell in a Jupyter notebook (.ipynb). Use instead of native NotebookEdit when the notebook is >5KB or has many unrelated cells — only the edited cell and its immediate neighbors are returned, with `[N cells unchanged]` for the rest. The full notebook is never echoed. Typical savings: 65-75% on multi-cell notebooks. Args: notebookPath, cellIndex, newSource, cellType (optional: code|markdown).

notebookPath.description: Absolute or cwd-relative path to the .ipynb notebook

cellIndex.description: Zero-based index of the cell to edit

newSource.description: New source content for the cell

cellType.description: Optional: change the cell type (code or markdown)

toolsWithPipe.name: ashlr__pipe
toolsWithPipe.description: [EXPERIMENTAL] Executes model-authored JS code server-side — off by default, enable with ASHLR_PIPE_ENABLE=1. Run a JS expression that calls ctx.{grep,read,ls,glob} internally — intermediate results NEVER enter context, only the return value does. Typical 80–95% token savings vs calling tools individually. ctx methods accept the same args as the ashlr__ tools they wrap. ctx.bash requires the additional ASHLR_PIPE_ALLOW_BASH=1 flag. Example: ctx.grep({pattern:'TODO',cwd:'.'}) returns the grep text as a string.

expr.description: Async function body (≤2000 chars). Receives `ctx` with grep/read/ls/glob methods (always available) and bash (requires ASHLR_PIPE_ALLOW_BASH=1). Return value is serialized as JSON. Blocked tokens: process, Bun, require, import(, globalThis, eval, fetch(, etc.

cwd.description: Working directory for cwd-relative tool calls (default: project root).

timeout_ms.description: Execution timeout in ms (default 10000, hard max 30000).

max_output_bytes.description: Truncate output to this many bytes (default 4096).

toolsWithPipe.name: ashlr__grep
toolsWithPipe.description: Search for a pattern. Use instead of native Grep always — genome-aware when .ashlrcode/genome/ exists (returns only the most relevant pre-summarized sections + merged PRs + closed issues), falls back to ripgrep with LLM summarization for large result sets. Compresses by filtering to relevant chunks; typical savings 70–90%.

bypassSummary.description: Skip LLM summarization, return rg output as-is (default: false)

include_prs.description: Include matching merged PRs from the cloud genome. Default: true. Set to false to skip PR retrieval entirely.

include_issues.description: Include matching closed issues from the cloud genome. Default: true. Set to false to skip issue retrieval entirely.

since_days.description: Optional freshness window — drop PRs / issues older than N days. Default: undefined (no filter).

toolsWithPipe.name: ashlr__edit
toolsWithPipe.description: Single literal search/replace in one file, returns only a diff summary. Use instead of native Edit when the file is >5KB or the combined before/after is >=80 chars — avoids the full file round-trip. Compresses by returning only the changed lines; typical savings 80%. In strict mode (default) requires exactly one match. For many edits across files use ashlr__multi_edit instead. For symbol renames use ashlr__edit_structural instead.

toolsWithPipe.name: ashlr__write
toolsWithPipe.description: Write content to a file without echoing the full content back. If the file already exists, delegates to ashlr__edit (full-file replace, compact diff response). If the file is new, creates it and returns a compact acknowledgment (path, bytes, sha8). Either way, the full file content is never returned — ~80% token savings vs native Write.

filePath.description: Absolute or cwd-relative path to write (`path` is accepted too)

toolsWithPipe.name: ashlr__http
toolsWithPipe.description: HTTP fetch with compressed output. Readable-extracts main content from HTML, pretty-prints + array-elides JSON, bounded byte cap. Refuses non-http/https schemes and private hosts by default.

toolsWithPipe.name: ashlr__logs
toolsWithPipe.description: Tail a log file efficiently. Reads the last N lines (default 200), detects severity from bracketed tags, bare prefixes, JSON/logfmt level fields, and Python tracebacks, filters by level and/or ISO timestamp, and collapses runs of identical consecutive lines into '(42x) ...'. Supports glob paths. Lines with no parseable timestamp are skipped (never fatal) when 'since' is set.

since.description: ISO timestamp — only lines after this

dedupe.description: Collapse repeated consecutive lines with count (default: true)

bypassSummary.description: If true, skip LLM summarization and return the full rendered log tail.

toolsWithPipe.name: ashlr__sql
toolsWithPipe.description: Run SQL against SQLite or Postgres and get a compact, token-dense text result. Replaces the typical 3-4 Bash calls (psql / sqlite3 + parse stdout) with one tool call. Supports SELECT, DDL, DML, EXPLAIN, and a schema-introspection mode.

query.description: SQL to run (SELECT, EXPLAIN, DDL, DML — all allowed). Required unless schema:true.

connection.description: Connection URL (postgres://…) or SQLite path. If omitted, reads $DATABASE_URL, then looks for *.db / *.sqlite files in cwd.

explain.description: Wrap in EXPLAIN ANALYZE (postgres) / EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN (sqlite). Default false.

limit.description: Max rows to return in the compact output (default 20). Total row count is always reported.

schema.description: Skip the query and instead list tables, columns, and row counts. Cheaper than many \d / SHOW TABLES round-trips.

bypassSummary.description: Skip LLM summarization of long output

toolsWithPipe.name: ashlr__diff_semantic
toolsWithPipe.description: AST-aware (heuristic) git diff summarization. A 200-line rename-refactor across 20 files renders as one line. Detects: symbol renames across >= 3 files, signature-only changes, formatting-only diffs. Degrades gracefully to compact diff output when no semantic patterns are found. Use instead of ashlr__diff when reviewing refactors, renames, or large reformatting commits.

range.description: Git range to diff, e.g. 'HEAD~1..HEAD'. Default: unstaged working tree changes.

staged.description: If true, diff staged changes (--cached). Overrides range.

bypassSummary.description: Skip LLM summarization of long semantic-diff output (default: false).

toolsWithPipe.name: ashlr__pr
toolsWithPipe.description: Fetch a GitHub PR and return a compact review-ready summary (header, reviews, unresolved comments, status checks). Read-only — never approves, comments, or merges. Saves 60-90% of the tokens a raw `gh pr view` dump would cost.

repo.description: owner/repo (default: auto-detect from cwd git remote)

mode.description: 'summary' (default: decisions + unresolved + checks) | 'full' (adds diff summary) | 'thread' (just comments)

toolsWithPipe.name: ashlr__issue
toolsWithPipe.description: Fetch a GitHub issue and return a compact header + body + comment list. In 'thread' mode, each comment is rendered with snipCompact on > 500 char bodies. Read-only.

repo.description: owner/repo (default: auto-detect from cwd git remote)

toolsWithPipe.name: ashlr__pr_comment
toolsWithPipe.description: Post a comment on a GitHub PR. Pass pr:"current" to target the PR for the checked-out branch. Returns the new comment URL.

pr.description: PR number or the string "current" to target the current branch's PR

repo.description: owner/repo (default: auto-detect from cwd git remote)

toolsWithPipe.name: ashlr__pr_approve
toolsWithPipe.description: Approve a GitHub PR with an optional review body. Refuses to approve your own PR. Pass pr:"current" to target the PR for the checked-out branch.

pr.description: PR number or the string "current" to target the current branch's PR

repo.description: owner/repo (default: auto-detect from cwd git remote)

toolsWithPipe.name: ashlr__issue_create
toolsWithPipe.description: Create a new GitHub issue with title + body and optional labels/assignees. Returns the new issue number and URL.

repo.description: owner/repo (default: auto-detect from cwd git remote)

toolsWithPipe.name: ashlr__issue_close
toolsWithPipe.description: Close a GitHub issue with an optional closing comment and reason (completed|not_planned).

repo.description: owner/repo (default: auto-detect from cwd git remote)

toolsWithPipe.name: ashlr__genome_propose
toolsWithPipe.description: Queue a proposed update to a named genome section. Fire-and-forget: the proposal is appended to the pending queue and will be merged into the genome on the next ashlr__genome_consolidate call. Use this to record project decisions, new strategies, architectural discoveries, or lessons learned so they persist across sessions.

section.description: Section path relative to .ashlrcode/genome, e.g. 'knowledge/decisions.md' or 'strategies/active.md'

content.description: Proposed content (full section replace OR appended block; see 'operation')

operation.description: How to apply the content (default: append)

toolsWithPipe.name: ashlr__genome_consolidate
toolsWithPipe.description: Merge pending proposals into the genome. Without `model` (and without $ASHLR_LLM_URL) runs a deterministic sequential-apply; with an LLM configured by $ASHLR_LLM_URL it merges conflicting proposals for the same section.

model.description: Pass 'none' to force offline sequential-apply, or any other value (for example 'llm') to merge with the LLM configured by $ASHLR_LLM_URL (default local LM Studio at 127.0.0.1:1234). The value is never used as an endpoint. If omitted, uses the LLM only when $ASHLR_LLM_URL or $ASHLR_LLM_KEY is set.

toolsWithPipe.name: ashlr__genome_status
toolsWithPipe.description: Show pending proposals and recent mutations for the current genome. Compact report suitable for inline context.

toolsWithPipe.name: ashlr__multi_edit
toolsWithPipe.description: Many edits across multiple files in one atomic call. Use instead of N separate Edit or ashlr__edit calls when touching more than one file — N round-trips collapse to 1, with full rollback on any failure. Compresses by returning one consolidated diff summary; typical savings (N−1) × per-call overhead. For a single file use ashlr__edit instead. For symbol renames use ashlr__edit_structural instead.

edits.description: Ordered list of edits to apply atomically.

path.description: Absolute or cwd-relative file path. File must exist.

search.description: Exact string to find in the file.

strict.description: Default true: require exactly one match (error if 0 or 2+). Pass false to replace all occurrences.

toolsWithPipe.name: ashlr__orient
toolsWithPipe.description: Meta-orientation tool. Answers 'how does X work here?' in a single call: runs a project tree scan, derives keywords from your query, discovers relevant files (genome retriever if .ashlrcode/genome/ exists, else ripgrep), snipCompacts them, and asks a local LLM for a ≤600-char synthesis plus a suggested next tool call. Replaces 3-5 round-trips (tree + grep + multiple reads). Read-only.

query.description: Question about the codebase: 'how does auth work', 'where is X defined', 'what's the deploy flow'

depth.description: 'quick' (1 tool call + 3 reads, ~2s) | 'thorough' (tree + grep + 6 reads, ~4s, default)

toolsWithPipe.name: ashlr__bash
toolsWithPipe.description: Run a shell command. Use instead of native Bash when the command produces verbose output (git log, test runners, npm install, find, ps). Auto-compresses stdout > 2KB and emits compact structured summaries for common commands (git status, ls, find, npm ls). stderr is never compressed. Refuses catastrophic patterns; use ashlr__read for cat. Typical savings 60–90% on verbose commands.

bypassSummary.description: Skip LLM summarization of long output

toolsWithPipe.name: ashlr__bash_start
toolsWithPipe.description: Spawn a long-running shell command in the background and return a session id. Use ashlr__bash_tail to poll incremental output, ashlr__bash_stop to kill, ashlr__bash_list to enumerate. Ideal for watchers, tails, long builds, and anything where streaming >> one-shot.

toolsWithPipe.name: ashlr__bash_tail
toolsWithPipe.description: Read new stdout/stderr since the last poll for a background session. Auto-compresses the tail window when > 2KB. If wait_ms > 0, blocks (event-driven) until output arrives or the process exits, up to that ceiling.

wait_ms.description: Block up to N ms for new output (default 1500; 0 = return immediately)

toolsWithPipe.name: ashlr__bash_stop
toolsWithPipe.description: Kill a background session by id. Sends SIGTERM (configurable) and escalates to SIGKILL after 2s if still alive.

signal.description: Default SIGTERM; escalates to SIGKILL after 2s

toolsWithPipe.name: ashlr__bash_list
toolsWithPipe.description: List active background sessions: id | pid | started | cumulative bytes | command.

toolsWithPipe.name: ashlr__test
toolsWithPipe.description: Run a test suite and return structured, token-efficient failure output. Supports bun test, vitest, jest, pytest, go test, and a generic fallback. Parses runner output into pass/fail/skip counts plus per-failure file:line + message + stack — eliminating the read-source-fix-rerun loop that wastes 25–30% of tokens on test-driven workflows.

command.description: Full command to run verbatim (e.g. 'bun test src/foo.test.ts'). Overrides runner + files.

cwd.description: Working directory (default: cwd). Must be inside the current cwd.

files.description: Specific test file paths to pass to the runner.

runner.description: Test runner to use. 'auto' detects from package.json / go.mod / pytest.ini (default: auto).

failuresOnly.description: Return only failure details, not per-test pass output (default: true).

bypassSummary.description: Show all failures instead of truncating at 2 inline (default: false).

watch.description: Run tests once, then fork into a background watch session that re-runs on .ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx/.py/.go file changes (debounced 200ms). Returns a session id — stream output with ashlr__bash_tail, stop with ashlr__bash_stop (default: false).

grep.description: Test name filter (informational label stored on the watch session).

toolsWithPipe.name: ashlr__savings
toolsWithPipe.description: Show estimated tokens and cost saved by ashlr tools in the current session and lifetime totals. Use instead of manually counting tool calls to measure ashlr efficiency.

toolsWithPipe.name: ashlr__ask
toolsWithPipe.description: Single-tool entry point for ashlr. Accepts a natural-language question and auto-routes to the correct underlying tool (ashlr__read, ashlr__grep, ashlr__orient, ashlr__tree, or ashlr__glob) using deterministic rules — no LLM in the routing step. Output always starts with a one-line trace showing which tool fired and why.
